title: The Death of Ivan Ilyich
text:
Ivan Ilyich Golovin had lived a correct, comfortable life as a judge in St. Petersburg. His marriage to Praskovya Fyodorovna had cooled into irritation, but he had his work, his card games and his well furnished flat. While hanging curtains in the new apartment, he slipped and knocked his side against a window frame. The bruise seemed nothing, but a pain began that would not go away.

As he grew worse, his family and doctors kept up a lie: that he was merely ill and would get better if he followed the treatment. He knew he was dying, and their pretense tormented him. His wife and daughter went to the theater and talked of engagements while he lay in agony, and he felt utterly alone.

The only one who comforted him was Gerasim, a young peasant servant. Gerasim did not pretend. He cleaned up after him without disgust and sat for hours holding Ivan's legs on his shoulders, the only position that eased the pain. Everyone dies some day, he said plainly, so why should he not take a little trouble for a sick man?

In his last hours, after three days of screaming, Ivan felt his young son kiss his hand and saw his wife's tear-stained face. He felt sorry for them and wanted to release them. The fear of death left him. Where death had been, there was light.
lesson: When someone we love is dying, honest presence comforts far more than polite pretending. Sometimes the bravest care is simply not to lie.
people: Ivan Ilyich Golovin, his wife Praskovya Fyodorovna, his son Vasya, the servant Gerasim
source: Leo Tolstoy, The Death of Ivan Ilyich (Smert Ivana Ilyicha), 1886
